title: The drive without a model
description: Owner 2026-11-08: solve the orchestrator. Design, probes and pass criterion: quality-gates-internal/plans/2026-11-08-orchestrator-without-model/PLAN.md. Prior art: plans/2026-11-05-cost-phase/analysis/prior-art-orchestrator.md.
desiredOutcome: A typed /audit:run, /audit:next or /audit:phase whose writer is a headless session runs the drive with no model request unless a step needs judgement or the human, so the orchestrator session stops being paid for relaying a script's output
summary: A typed /audit:run or /audit:phase whose writer is a headless session now runs the drive from a UserPromptSubmit hook with no model request unless a step needs judgement or the human; a hook failure, plan mode, Windows and /audit:next leave the command as it was. Three review rounds; fixes are P159.3 to P159.5.

tasks.title: drive-phase.py auto runs the drive's mechanical steps itself and ends with a distinct answer on done, on stop, and on a step that needs a model
tasks.description: Today the main loop is a model executing: next --signal, next --explain, run the printed run: line in background Bash, repeat (orchestrator's calls in stage-2 re-measurement k02m-k07mr, 12 to 23 per task, none carrying a decision). Add an `auto` action beside `next` in build_parser (drive-phase.py ~11769) that takes the same target forms and --task. Reuse the step result `next` builds (the signal dict in the function near 11610: step, subject, basis, next, runs, prompts) instead of parsing printed lines, and classify a step through SIGNAL_VERBS (859): done/stop end; judge/ask/review end as needs-model; dispatch with runs is executed; dispatch with no runs (an Agent) is needs-model; wait is resolved by the fact that auto itself ran the child to exit. Do not route through a shell a command the drive built, keep it an argv. wait-writer's docstring says only the main loop knows whether a session started: auto is that main loop now, so say what it knows. Exit answers are three distinct codes, documented in --help, and stdout on done/stop is what --explain prints, bounded as it is. No model is involved, so nothing here may be a new decision: every branch that the model used to take on `judge`/`ask` stays the model's or the human's. A gate's and a writer's run is a child of auto in its own process group; SIGTERM (what Esc delivers to a hook, probed 2026-11-08) is forwarded and auto exits with the stop answer, leaving the in-progress task for `next` to resume. The Bash foreground bound and gate_in_background do not apply inside auto, but leave that choice's readers intact. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: A UserPromptSubmit hook runs the drive for a typed run verb and blocks the prompt only when the drive finished without needing a model
tasks.description: Probed on claude 2.1.319 (PLAN.md table): a UserPromptSubmit hook printing {"decision":"block","reason":...} ends `claude -p "/x:y"` with exit 0, total_cost_usd 0, num_turns 0, and the reason in result; a hook lived 720 s with timeout 1800 and could start a nested claude -p; interactively the CLI shows a spinner with esc to interrupt, and Esc is SIGTERM to the hook. The hook receives the prompt as typed. Docs: default timeout on this event is 30 s, so set timeout explicitly; on timeout the prompt still reaches Claude unless onFailure is "block"; reason is not added to context; hookSpecificOutput.suppressOriginalPrompt drops the "Original prompt:" tail. Hooks are importless of scripts/: resolve through hooks/_config.find_script(), launched via py-launch.sh like the others. It fires on every prompt of every session, so the prefilter for "not one of our verbs" is a string check before anything heavy, under the bench-hooks budget; SECURITY.md's fail-mode table is held by gate-parity. Fail-open here means the prompt goes on to the model and the command runs as it does today, which is safe because the drive's own lock and state decide. A new config key (default on) turns it off; adding a key is free under COMPATIBILITY.md. The command texts run.md, next.md and phase.md state the pass-through case: when the prompt reaches the model, the drive may already have advanced, so it continues with next. Check how /audit:next picks its task (audit-status READY NOW, commands/next.md) and reuse that reading rather than a second rule; if it needs a model, say why and leave that verb passing through. The run-agent-session environment scrub (PARENT_SESSION_VARS) already covers a child started from a hook; confirm rather than assume. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: A wave runs under auto only when every member is a dispatch with a command, a step owing a board echo goes to the model, and an unreaped child or a closed terminal ends the drive honestly
tasks.description: Phase code review of P159 (two read-only opus reviewers; each case below was run by the reviewer with the real driver and a stub claude). (1) drive-phase.py step_member (~7806) returns "dispatch" for any non-decide member, so inside a wave a wait-writer, wait-gate, wait-reviewer-session or follow-browser arrives at auto_answer (~11838) as a dispatch and its run: command is started again: a SIGKILLed session runner at waveWidth 2 started claude 6 times against 1 at width 1, and a follow-browser recipe is dropped. Classify by member: a wave is executed only when every member is a dispatch with a run: command; anything else ends needs-model and starts nothing. (2) ado_echo_lines (~11639) reads one step, and auto discards every step's text but the last, so an earlier task's board update is lost and on a done ending no model performs the last. A step that owes an echo ends needs-model, carrying it, so the existing command text does it; warnings a step said (a cancelled gate, a refused note, cannot-tell) reach the final text within the existing bound. (3) auto_report (~11902) raises TypeError on a child whose returncode is None, turning an interrupt into exit 2 with empty stdout; say the run was not reaped. (4) A direct auto arms no SIGHUP: closing a terminal leaves children running in their own sessions; arm it. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: The prompt hook never stops ordinary work when it cannot run, does not start another task after an interrupt, drives the tree the command drives, and stands aside in plan mode
tasks.description: Phase code review of P159. (1) Probed on claude 2.1.319: a hook command that cannot start under onFailure "block" blocks every prompt with cost 0, ahead of the prefilter, with no writerModel set. A plugin update under an open session or an empty CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT would stop all work, against SECURITY.md, the README and py-launch.sh. Remove onFailure; a failed hook sends the prompt on, which is the command as it was. The timeout stays long enough that expiry is not a normal path; state what expiry then does, and make the drive stop when its parent goes rather than run on. (2) /audit:next picks ready[0], which excludes in_progress, so after any interrupt or needs-model stop retyping it starts a different task (run: P1.1 and P1.2 both in_progress, a paid session on the wrong one), and a pending decision is a dead end. When the plan holds a task in progress, /audit:next passes through and next.md rule continues it; the interrupt line stops promising a resume the hook does not do. Fix next.md order so the "no ready task" rule does not pre-empt the in-progress paragraph. (3) Read the parent pid before anything that can take a signal: Esc during audit-status orphans a whole paid drive. (4) repo_root reads CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR before cwd, so the hook and the pass-through command can drive different trees from a linked worktree; resolve the tree one way, through _config.tree_for. (5) permission_mode plan passes through: plan mode is read-only intent and the hook would start paid writers and commit. A Bash deny rule is not read: state that in SECURITY.md with the opt-out key rather than parsing rules. (6) Windows: proc.terminate() is TerminateProcess, so auto cannot tear down and its writers survive; use taskkill /T /F there, keep the parent-gone check honest (getppid does not change on Windows), qualify the CHANGELOG line, and name the Windows command for a manual check since the cases skip there. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.

tasks.title: The prompt hook acts only when the prompt names its target, resolves the tree the command resolves, and stands aside on Windows until a stop is proven there
tasks.description: Second review round of P159. The recurrences have one root each, so these are invariants rather than more shapes. (1) /audit:next chooses its target from state the drive itself changes: after an echo-owing close it ran a second paid task or stranded the echo and the phase lock (run with a stub claude), after the earlier interrupt and pending-decision fixes. The hook acts only when the prompt names its target: /audit:run <id> and /audit:phase <id>. Remove /audit:next from the table and everything only it used (first_ready and the audit-status read); /audit:next passes through and runs as it did. next.md goes back to its previous rules except for what still applies. (2) The hook and the command must resolve the same tree: from a cwd in <main>/.claude/worktrees/x with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR=<main> the hook drove and committed on main while the command resolves the worktree (_config within_root answers before git; tree_for docstring names this residual). Bash has no CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR, so the command's drive-phase.py project_context reads cwd. The hook starts auto from the session cwd with CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR removed and no --project-dir, so auto resolves by the one reader the command uses, and the hook reads the writerModel setting from that same tree. Whatever cannot be told to agree passes through. (3) Windows cannot deliver SIGTERM to another process, so Esc ends only the launcher and auto and its writers keep spending; parent_gone cannot see it and taskkill is unreachable from that path. Until a real Windows run proves a stop, the hook passes through on Windows, so the command runs as it did. Remove the Windows stop branch this makes dead, and state the limit in SECURITY.md, the README and the CHANGELOG. No F/P/BUG ids in comments.
